{{nihongo foot|'''''Donkey Kong Jr. Math'''''|ドンキーコングJR.の算数遊び|Donkī Kongu Junia no Sansū Asobi|lead=yes|group=lower-alpha}} is a 1983 [[edutainment]] [[Platform game|platform]] [[video game]] developed and published by [[Nintendo]] for the [[Nintendo Entertainment System]]. It is a [[Spin-off (media)|spin-off]] of the 1982 arcade game ''[[Donkey Kong Jr.]]'' In the game, players control [[Donkey Kong Jr. (character)|Donkey Kong Jr.]] as he solves math problems set up by his father [[Donkey Kong (character)|Donkey Kong]].

It is the only game in the Education Series of NES games in North America, owing to the game's lack of success. It was made available in various forms, including in the 2002 [[GameCube]] video game ''[[Animal Crossing (video game)|Animal Crossing]]'' and on the [[Virtual Console]] services for [[Wii]] and [[Wii U]] in 2007 and 2014 respectively, and in 2024 for the [[Nintendo Classics]] service. ''Donkey Kong Jr. Math'' was a critical and commercial failure. It has received criticism from several publications including ''[[IGN]]'' staff, who called it one of the worst Virtual Console games.

Bruce Lowry, Nintendo of America’s vice president of sales from 1981 to 1986, referred to it as “the worst game we ever sold.”<ref>{{Cite web | title=MSN | url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/technology/former-nintendo-vp-of-sales-reflects-on-their-worst-game-ever/ar-AA1OE8Kh?ocid=msedgntp&pc=U531&cvid=68f4142f1890470f800a3b11d9ced431&ei=16 | access-date=2026-08-31 | website=www.msn.com}}</ref>

==Gameplay==
[[File:Donkey Kong Jr. Math.jpg|thumb|left|230px|Two players compete by creating arithmetic equations to reach the number held by Donkey Kong (top center). Player 1 (middle left) climbs vines to acquire numbers. Player 2 (bottom right) stands on its starting platform.]]
The game features two modes, one single-player and the other allowing for one to two players.<ref name="ag" /><ref name="ign" /> Its mechanics are similar to its predecessor, ''Donkey Kong Jr.''<ref name="ag" /> The Calculate mode has Donkey Kong hold up a number, which players must attempt to reach by collecting a combination of digits and arithmetic symbols to eventually reach that number.<ref name="ag" /> Players must climb vines to reach these figures.<ref name=gspot/> The +−×÷ Exercise requires players to solve fixed math puzzles by climbing chains to reach the correct numbers and arithmetic symbols to do so.<ref name="ag" /><ref name=gspot/>

== Development ==
{{further|Donkey Kong Jr.#Development}}
''Donkey Kong Jr. Math'' was developed by [[Nintendo Research & Development 2]] and designed by Toshihiko Nakago.<ref name="iwata">{{Cite web |last=Iwata |first=Satoru |title=It All Begin in 1984 |url=http://iwataasks.nintendo.com/interviews/#/wii/nsmb/1/0 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130816051935/http://iwataasks.nintendo.com/interviews/#/wii/nsmb/1/0 |archive-date=August 16, 2013 |access-date=September 22, 2019 |website=[[Iwata Asks]]}}</ref> It was published by [[Nintendo]] for the [[Family Computer]] (Famicom) and [[Nintendo Entertainment System]] (NES).<ref name="iwata" /><ref name="ign2" /> It reuses its engine, assets, and gameplay from ''Donkey Kong Jr.''<ref name="polygon" /><ref name="ag" /><ref name=gspot/> It was a part of the Educational Series on the NES, a series that was originally supposed to have three entries, including music game {{nihongo foot|'''''Donkey Kong's Music Play'''''| ドンキーコングの音楽遊び|Donkī Kongu no Ongaku Asobi|lead=yes|group=lower-alpha}} [[:ja:ドンキーコングJR.の算数遊び#ドンキーコングの音楽遊び|[ja]]], but was the only one released under that line.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Parish |first=Jeremy |date=June 27, 2017 |title=What Does Star Fox 2's Resurrection Mean for Other Lost Games? |url=https://retronauts.com/article/416/what-does-star-fox-2s-resurrection-mean-for-other-lost-games |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190607003221/https://retronauts.com/article/416/what-does-star-fox-2s-resurrection-mean-for-other-lost-games |archive-date=June 7, 2019 |access-date=September 1, 2019 |website=[[Retronauts]]}}</ref> A lack of success by the game was attributed by a Nintendo spokesman to be the reason Nintendo did not make more educational titles.<ref name="latimes" /> It was the first spin-off title Nintendo made.<ref name="ign2" />

The game was first released in Japan on December 12, 1983, and was released shortly after together with ''Donkey Kong Jr.'' as a licensed [[multicart]] (released in a bundle together with [[Sharp Corporation|Sharp]]'s [[C1 Famicom TV]]).<ref name="nl">{{Cite web |last=McFerran |first=Damien |date=April 20, 2007 |title=Donkey Kong Jr. Math Review (NES) |url=http://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/vc/donkey_kong_jr_math_nes |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190503203853/http://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/vc/donkey_kong_jr_math_nes |archive-date=May 3, 2019 |access-date=September 22, 2019 |website=[[Nintendo Life]]}}</ref><ref name="famitsu11aug95">''NEWSCLUB Premium Goods プレミアム グッズ - プレミア付、ってだけで興味あるでしょ? : 金では売れん自慢の一品''. [[Famicom Tsūshin]]. No.347. Pg.179. 11 August 1995.</ref> In August 1995, the Sharp multicart was re-released separately from the C1 Famicom TV.<ref name=famitsu11aug95/> The game has been released on other platforms, including the video game ''[[Animal Crossing (video game)|Animal Crossing]]'', which featured several NES games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Donkey Kong Jr. Math (GameCube Download) - Game Boy Advance - GameSpy |url=http://gba.gamespy.com/gameboy-advance/donkey-kong-jr-math-n-port/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110711072216/http://gba.gamespy.com/gameboy-advance/donkey-kong-jr-math-n-port/ |archive-date=July 11, 2011 |access-date=October 15, 2010 |website=[[GameSpy]]}}</ref> ''Donkey Kong Jr. Math'' was re-released on the [[Wii]]'s [[Virtual Console]] in Japan on March 27, 2007,<ref>{{Cite web |title=VC ドンキーコングJR.の算数遊び |url=https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_dkm/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150426173234/http://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_dkm/ |archive-date=April 26, 2015 |access-date=May 30, 2015 |website=Nintendo.co.jp |publisher=[[Nintendo]] |language=ja}}</ref> Europe and Australia on April 20, and in North America on September 3.<ref name="nl" /> It was re-released again for the [[Wii U]]'s [[Virtual Console]] in North America on August 28, 2014, in Europe on January 22, 2015, and in Japan on April 15.<ref name="nl" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=ドンキーコングJR.の算数遊び |url=https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_dkm/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150426173234/http://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_dkm/ |archive-date=April 26, 2015 |access-date=May 30, 2015 |website=Nintendo.co.jp |publisher=[[Nintendo]] |language=ja}}</ref>

==Reception==
{{Video game reviews
| GR = 32%<ref name="Gamerankings">{{Cite web |date=June 24, 2013 |title=Donkey Kong Jr. Math for Nes |url=http://www.gamerankings.com/nes/587235-donkey-kong-jr-math/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130624212148/http://www.gamerankings.com/nes/587235-donkey-kong-jr-math/index.html |archive-date=June 24, 2013 |access-date=August 11, 2013 |website=[[GameRankings]]}}</ref>
| Allgame = 3/5<ref name="ag">{{Cite web |last=Miller |first=Skyler |title=Donkey Kong Jr. Math - Overview |url=http://allgame.com/game.php?id=22152&tab=review |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100102104359/http://allgame.com/game.php?id=22152 |archive-date=January 2, 2010 |access-date=May 29, 2013 |website=[[AllGame]]}}</ref>
| EuroG = 3/10<ref name="eurog" />
| GSpot = 3/10<ref name="gspot">{{Cite web |last=Provo |first=Frank |date=September 3, 2007 |title=Donkey Kong Jr. Math Review for Wii |url=http://www.gamespot.com/wii/puzzle/donkeykongjrmath/review.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070915230530/http://www.gamespot.com/wii/puzzle/donkeykongjrmath/review.html |archive-date=September 15, 2007 |access-date=October 15, 2010 |website=[[GameSpot]]}}</ref>
| IGN = 3/10<ref name="ign" />
| NLife = 1/10<ref name="nl" />
}}

''Donkey Kong Jr. Math'' was met with negative reviews from the press.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Benson |first=Roy Michael |date=December 2014 |title=Games Based Learning |url=http://wrap.warwick.ac.uk/76586/1/WRAP_THESIS_Benson_2014.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170309062122/http://wrap.warwick.ac.uk/76586/1/WRAP_THESIS_Benson_2014.pdf |archive-date=March 9, 2017 |access-date=September 21, 2019 |website=Wrap.Warwick.ac.uk}}</ref><ref name="Gamerankings" /> Despite this negative reception, the magazine ''Joystick'' felt Nintendo was worthy of praise for its attempt at making an educational game.<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=January 1989 |title=Donkey Kong Jr. Math Review |magazine=Joystick |page=84}}</ref> The game was also a commercial failure, with a Nintendo spokesperson noting its lack of success as being due to poor reception.<ref name="latimes">{{Cite news |last=Hunt |first=Dennis |date=July 27, 1990 |title=Nintendo: Kids Just Want to Have Fun |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1990-07-27-ca-805-story.html |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=2024-03-09 |archive-date=2024-03-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240309032206/https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1990-07-27-ca-805-story.html |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Donkey Kong Jr. Math'' performed better in Japan but was forgotten in the United States.<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=November 1994 |title=From Video-Game Villain to SGI Spokesmodel |magazine=Video Games |page=70 |issue=70}}</ref> Its poor sales contributed to it becoming a rare and expensive collector's item.<ref name="polygon">{{Cite web |last=Parish |first=Jeremy |date=May 10, 2018 |title=The Definitive Ranking of Donkey Kong Games |url=https://www.polygon.com/features/2018/5/10/17333228/donkey-kong-rankings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190403080041/https://www.polygon.com/features/2018/5/10/17333228/donkey-kong-rankings |archive-date=April 3, 2019 |access-date=September 22, 2019 |website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]}}</ref>

Jeremy Parish of ''[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]'' called it the worst ''Donkey Kong'' video game, suggesting that it was a "half-finished game" to have a larger launch lineup on the Famicom.<ref name="polygon" /> He was also critical of the reuse of assets from ''Donkey Kong Jr.'', while Skyler Miller of ''[[AllGame]]'' found this reuse creative.<ref name="polygon" /><ref name="ag" /> Bob Mackey of ''[[1UP.com]]'' called ''Donkey Kong Jr. Math'' the worst NES launch window title, criticizing it for its lack of value and sluggish movement.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mackey|first=Bob |title=The Most Explosively Awful Console Launch Titles from 1UP.com |url=http://www.1up.com/do/feature?cId=3167419 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090304054407/http://www.1up.com/do/feature?cId=3167419 |archive-date=March 4, 2009 |access-date=October 15, 2010 |website=[[1UP.com]]}}</ref> The game had a poor reception from ''[[IGN]]'', with Lucas M. Thomas finding its controls and execution poor,<ref name="ign">{{Cite web |last=Thomas|first=Lucas M. |date=September 6, 2007 |title=Donkey Kong Jr. Math Review - Wii Review at IGN |url=http://wii.ign.com/articles/818/818013p1.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071016075533/http://wii.ign.com/articles/818/818013p1.html |archive-date=October 16, 2007 |access-date=October 15, 2010 |website=[[IGN]]}}</ref> while Cam Shea regarded it as one of the worst Virtual Console games and criticized it for a lack of value.<ref name="ign2">{{Cite web |last=Shea |first=Cam |date=August 7, 2008 |title=The Worst Games on Virtual Console: Part 1 - Wii Feature at IGN |url=http://wii.ign.com/articles/897/897106p1.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101213123010/http://wii.ign.com/articles/897/897106p1.html |archive-date=December 13, 2010 |access-date=October 15, 2010 |website=[[IGN]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Shea |first=Cam |date=April 23, 2007 |title=Virtual Console AU Buyer's Guide - Part 4 - Wii Feature at IGN |url=http://wii.ign.com/articles/782/782613p1.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100831011442/http://wii.ign.com/articles/782/782613p1.html |archive-date=August 31, 2010 |access-date=October 15, 2010 |website=[[IGN]]}}</ref> Dan Whitehead of ''[[Eurogamer]]'' similarly could not justify the asking price for the Virtual Console version.<ref name="eurog">{{Cite web |last=Whitehead |first=Dan|date=June 2, 2007 |title=Virtual Console Roundup Wii Review - Page 3 |url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/r_vcroundup010607_wii?page=3 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121006022338/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/r_vcroundup010607_wii?page=3 |archive-date=October 6, 2012 |access-date=October 15, 2010 |website=[[Eurogamer]]}}</ref> Frank Provo of ''[[GameSpot]]'' felt that its math problems were either too easy for young children or too boring for older ones.<ref name=gspot/> Damien McFarren of ''[[Nintendo Life]]'' criticized the game for "shoehorning" education into this game and for poor controls.<ref name="nl">{{Cite web |last=McFerran |first=Damien |date=April 20, 2007 |title=Donkey Kong Jr. Math Review (NES) |url=http://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/vc/donkey_kong_jr_math_nes |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190503203853/http://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/vc/donkey_kong_jr_math_nes |archive-date=May 3, 2019 |access-date=September 22, 2019 |website=[[Nintendo Life]]}}</ref> Author Jeff Ryan referred to the game as a "dud". While noting that it "reinforced math fundamentals", he called the gameplay "fun" but "challenging".<ref>{{Cite book |last=Ryan |first=Jeff |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1k-6ksl3uLsC |title=Super Mario: How Nintendo Conquered America |publisher=[[Penguin Publishing Group]] |year=2011 |isbn=978-1101517635 |page=84}}</ref>

''Donkey Kong Jr. Math'' has received criticism for its qualities as an educational game. Elizabeth Sweedyk, associate computer science professor at [[Harvey Mudd College]], felt that ''Donkey Kong Jr. Math'' was too realistic an educational game to be fun.<ref name="inside">{{Cite web |last=David Epstein |date=October 26, 2005 |title=News: Joystick Nation - Inside Higher Ed |url=http://www.insidehighered.com/news/2005/10/26/games?no_mobile_redirect=true |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121001215346/http://www.insidehighered.com/news/2005/10/26/games?no_mobile_redirect=true |archive-date=October 1, 2012 |access-date=October 15, 2010 |website=[[Inside Higher Ed]]}}</ref> Kevin Gifford of ''1UP.com'' felt that it lacks appeal for children, while Frank Caron for ''[[Ars Technica]]'' felt it inferior to other educational games like ''[[Brain Age]]'' and ''[[Math Blaster]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wrecking Crew (Famicom Mini 14) Review for from 1UP.com |url=http://www.1up.com/do/reviewPage?cId=3128754 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120719051003/http://www.1up.com/do/reviewPage?cId=3128754 |archive-date=July 19, 2012 |access-date=October 15, 2010 |website=[[1UP.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Caron |first=Frank |date=September 3, 2007 |title=Virtual Console Monday (9-03-07): A Labor Day Foursome |url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/news/2007/09/virtual-console-monday-9-03-07-a-labor-day-foursome.ars |access-date=October 15, 2010 |website=[[Ars Technica]] |archive-date=August 6, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240806052828/https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2007/09/virtual-console-monday-9-03-07-a-labor-day-foursome/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
